name: Puerto Rican Vireo
rangeDescription: Confined mainly to limestone hills of western and central puerto rico
description: A small, noisy inhabitant of woodlands including mangrove swamps and shade coffee plantations; often feeds low, near ground. This relatively plain species has a grayish head and chest that contrasts with a yellow-washed belly.

name: Brown-breasted Barbet
rangeDescription: Savanna of southern somalia to kenya, southeastern malawi, and northern mozambique
description: Large and unusually colored barbet, with a mostly red head, a broad brown band across the underparts, a black back, and a white belly and rump patch. Also note the chunky pale bill.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Prairie Falcon
rangeDescription: Arid north america (british columbia to northern mexico)
description: Large, brown-and-white falcon of dry, open areas in western North America. Pale brown above and white below, with dark streaks and prominent mustache.

name: Buff-winged Cinclodes
rangeDescription: Southern chile and southern argentina; winters to southeastern brazil, uruguay, and paraguay
description: Fairly common in southern South America, from bogs and streams in the Andes to beaches, lakeshores, and pastures; usually near water. Feeds on the ground with a hopping and shuffling gait, sometimes cocking tail; small flocks form in migration and winter.

name: Sierra Nevada Brushfinch
rangeDescription: Santa marta mountains (northeastern colombia)
description: Shy and skulking brushfinch restricted to cloud forest in Colombia’s Santa Marta Mountains. Quite distinctive in its limited range, with a black face and breast spot, white throat, and striped head.

name: Andaman Wood-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Andaman and nicobar islands
description: A large pigeon with dark gray upperparts and pale gray head and underparts. Note the pale yellow bill, the reddish bare skin around the eye, and the silvery neck with blackish bars.

name: Alta Floresta Antpitta
rangeDescription: Amazonian brazil (south of the amazon river, between the madeira and the xingu)
description: Secretive species, almost tailless with long legs. Has a black-spotted breast, white throat, and conspicuous buff “goggles”.

name: Lord Howe Rail
rangeDescription: Highlands of lord howe island (endangered)
description: A long-necked and short-tailed rail with a long decurved bill. Uniformly brownish red, sometimes with variable barring on underside and flanks.

name: Gray-chested Babbler
rangeDescription: Southeastern nigeria to southern cameroon, eastern democratic republic of the congo, and western kenya; bioko
description: Unusual thrush-like bird with bright reddish-brown upperparts and gray underparts. Found in the understory of montane forest, often in thick and moist areas.

name: Rufous-tailed Hawk
rangeDescription: Patagonian forest of southern chile and argentina
description: Scarce and often rather local hawk of temperate rainforest and edge, adjacent open and semiopen areas. Looks similar to the Red-tailed Hawk of North America.

name: Rufous-headed Chachalaca
rangeDescription: Western ecuador and far northwestern peru
description: Large chickenlike bird with a long tail. No similar species in limited range; much smaller than Crested Guan and warmer brown than Sickle-winged Guan.

name: Striped Crake
rangeDescription: Locally in sub-saharan africa
description: Small brown crake with conspicuous striping on the back. The underparts are brown in the male and gray in the female.

name: Chachapoyas Antpitta
rangeDescription: East slope of the andes of northern peru (amazonas south of the río marañón, southward to huánuco, and north of the río huallaga)
description: Rotund bird with long legs and a short tail, endemic to the eastern Andes of northern Peru. Plumage is mostly brown with an orange tinge to the underparts.

name: Gray-crested Helmetshrike
rangeDescription: Dry thornscrub of southwestern kenya and western tanzania
description: A sociable, cartoon-like black-and-white helmetshrike with a tall and fluffy gray crest, piercing yellow eyes, and small black patches on the sides of the breast. The black-and-white contrast is most apparent in flight, with white patches in the outer wing and at the end of the tail.

name: Sumichrast's Wren
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southern mexico (veracruz, puebla, and adjacent northern oaxaca)
description: Very local in humid evergreen forest of limestone (karst) lowlands and foothills in northern Oaxaca and adjacent Veracruz; endemic. Stays on or near the ground, moving quickly among limestone boulders, popping in and out of caves and crevices.

name: Pringle's Puffback
rangeDescription: Ethiopia and somalia to kenya and northeastern tanzania
description: A small bushshrike in which males and females are strikingly different. Males are black and gray on the upperparts, whitish below.

name: Bay-ringed Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (espírito santo) to eastern paraguay and northeastern argentina
description: Small flycatcher with a long slender tail, which is often held cocked. Note the diagnostic cinnamon patches around the eyes contrasting with a green head, pale eye, and yellow throat.

name: Rufous-throated Tanager
rangeDescription: Andes of western colombia and western ecuador (southward to el oro)
description: Distinctive small tanager with mostly black head, orange throat, and bold black spotting on underparts. Upperparts are dark with a scaled look.

name: White-gaped Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Northern australia (king sound, western australia to townsville, queensland)
description: A medium to large honeyeater with a sooty brown plumage and a bright pale patch between its eye and bill. Much larger than the similarly colored Dusky Honeyeater.

name: Mauritius White-eye
rangeDescription: Highlands of mauritius (western mascarene islands)
description: An unusual white-eye with dark plumage and a long, curved bill. Mostly gray with an olive-green wing and rump and a broad white eye-ring.
